High level of Ammonia in Yamuna water
2698. SHRI ANAND SHARMA:  Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that the dangerous rise in Ammonia levels in 
raw water supply from Yamuna, has resulted in reduction of potable water production 
in the national capital;
(b) if so, the impact of high Ammonia levels on supply of safe drinking water; 
(c) the impact on health due to dangerous level of Ammonia in drinking water 
along with the treating agent Chlorine; and 
(d) whether Government has prepared an action plan to address the challenge 
of high Ammonia level and to ensure supply of safe drinking water to the city?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION (DR. SATYA PAL SINGH): 
(a) and (b) Delhi Jal Board (DJB) supplies approx. 900 Million Gallon per Day 
(MGD) of water to consumers in Delhi. The source of raw water for Delhi is from 
rivers Yamuna and Ganga. The conveyance of Yamuna and Ganga raw water is done 
through carrier lined channel and Delhi sub-branch and conduits from upper Ganga 
canal respectively. About 65 MGD is lifted directly from River Yamuna (Wazirabad 
Pond), upstream of Wazirabad Barrage. The level of ammonia in the water lifted 

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [20 March, 2018]   ...for the  19 March, 2018 283
directly from Wazirabad Pond from 31.12.2017 was found to be in the range of 1.5 
to 2.6 Parts Per Million (PPM) which is beyond the treatable limits of the concerned 
water treatment plants of DJB. Ammonia level being higher than the treatable limit 
in the water directly being lifted from river Yamuna (Wazirabad Pond), drinking 
water supply in some parts of Delhi has been affected to some extent. 
(c) and (d) High Ammonia Level in potable water leads to increase in chlorine 
demand. High level of ammonia is generally associated with high level of Bio 
Chemical Oxygen Demand (Bio degradable organic matter). Chlorine in presence of 
organic matter may form tri-halo methane (THM) which can have harmful impact. 
The cleaning of rivers is an ongoing process and this Ministry is supplementing 
the efforts of the States for checking the rising level of pollution of river Yamuna, 
a tributary of River Ganga, by providing financial assistance to States of Haryana, 
Delhi and Uttar Pradesh in phased manner since 1993 under the Yamuna Action 
Plan (YAP). The total expenditure incurred on conservation of river Yamuna under 
the YAP Phase-I and II is ` 1514.70.
At present, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) assisted YAP  
Phase-III project is under implementation at an estimated cost of ` 1656 crore in 
Delhi for rehabilitation and up-gradation of existing Sewage Treatment Plants (950 
Million Litres Per Day) and Trunk sewers (43 kms) in Delhi. Delhi Jal Board (DJB) 
is the implementing agency. The duration of YAP-III project is 7 years. As part 
of various steps to clean river Yamuna under the Hon’ble National Green Tribunal 
(NGT)’s Maily Se Nirmal Yamuna Revitalization Plan 2017, Phase-I, the Ministry has 
sanctioned the Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) works in command area of Najafgarh 
Drain (Dhansa to Keshopur) in Delhi for an estimated amount of ` 344.81 crore. 
In addition to these, following projects have been undertaken by State Government 
of Delhi for addressing the problem of pollution of river Yamuna:–
 ● Construction of 318 MLD (70 Million gallons per day) STP with 10 years 
Operation and Maintenance (O&M) on at Coronation Pillar. 
 ● Construction of 15 MGD (68.1 MLD) Waste Water Treatment Plant at Delhi 
Gate drain.
 ● Construction of 7 decentralised Waste Water Treatment Plant in Najafgarh 
Zone. 
 ● Laying of Sewer lines in unauthorised colonies.
 ● Rehabilitation of 3 Peripheral Sewer lines. 
Further, two projects “STP and Sewerage works” in Sonepat and Panipat towns

Namami Gange as long term project
†2701. SHRI LAL SINH V ADODIA: Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION be pleased to state:

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION (DR. SATYA PAL SINGH): 
(a) to (c) Namami Gange Programme covers short term, medium term and long 
term activities. Under short term activities, certain entry level activities which cover 
development of ghats and crematoria, river surface cleaning activities etc. have been 
planned. Under medium term activities, existing sewage treatment plant and effluent 
treatment plant will be upgraded and new Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) and Effluent

up in the villages on the bank of river Ganga. The long term action plan involves 
restoration of wholesomeness of river Ganga, and maintaining the ecological and 
geological integrity of river.
Government of India has launched Namami Gange Programme in May, 2015 for 
conservation of river Ganga with total outlay of ` 20,000 crores. Namami Gange 
Programme is a holistic approach to clean Ganga through various activities such as 
treatment of municipal sewage, treatment of industrial effluent, river surface cleaning, 
rural sanitation, ghats and crematoria works, afforestation, biodiversity conservation, 
awareness creation and public outreach etc. Under Namami Gange Program, a total 
of 189 projects for these various activities have been sanctioned, out of which,  
48 projects have been completed so far and others are at various stages of execution/
implementation. It has been planned to complete these projects by 2020.

MEGHWAL): (a) and (b) River Bhutahi Balan flows from hilly region of Nepal and 
enters in Bihar at Laokaha in Khutauna Block of Madhubani District of Bihar. Due

An embankment of length of 34.11 km is already constructed on right side of

to Nirmali-Ghoghardiha-link road. In case of sudden high discharge in river, the water 
spreads into nearby areas through this open gap of 5.50 Km. into villages Suryahi, 
Ramnagar, Chithrumandal, Dhankhor, Parsa, Labtol etc. but, this water stays for a 
short period and flows through the passage provided in Nirmali-Ghoghardiha link 
road and railway line and finally join Kosi river.

Project for the capacity augmentation of navigation on the Haldia-Varanasi stretch 
of National Waterway-1 (Ganga) with the technical and financial assistance of the 
World Bank at an estimated cost of ` 5,369.18 crore.
Under this project construction of three multimodal terminals, one intermodal 
terminal, one new navigational lock, River Information Stations (RIS) has commenced. 
Vessel repair and maintenance facilities, Ro-Ro terminals are also envisaged. The 
objective of the project is to facilitate transportation of goods on Ganga from Uttar 
Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.
A Protocol on Inland Water Trade and Transit (PIWTT) between India and 
Bangladesh exists to facilitate movement of cargo from India to Bangladesh and 
also to North East Region of India. River Brahmaputra (NW-2) and river Barak 
(NW-16) are connected with NW-1 through Sundarbans waterways (NW-97) and 
rivers of Bangladesh. 
Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is developing two stretches 
viz. Sirajganj-Daikhawa and Ashuganj-Zakiganj in Bangladesh at a total cost of  
` 305.84 crore on 80 : 20 cost sharing basis (80% being borne by India and 20% by 
Bangladesh). The development of these two stretches will provide critical connectivity 
to the North-East region through the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route.

Reservoir level in Bhakra and Pong dams
2705. SHRI RAMKUMAR VERMA:  Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Bhakra and Pong dams are not filled up to the 
Full Reservoir Level (FRL); 
(b) if so, whether by use of latest technology, better planning and forecasting, 
dams could be filled up to FRL; 
(c) whether Government intends to give directions to Bhakhra Beas Management 
Board to carry out the study regarding the decision for maximum levels of Bhakra 
and Pong dam reservoirs; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION (SHRI ARJUN RAM 
MEGHWAL): (a) and (b) The Bhakra and Pong Reservoirs are filled up to Full 
Reservoir Level (FRL) based on actual availability/inflows of water. However, after 
the devastating floods during the year 1988, Government of India in March, 1989, 
constituted a Committee to report on the problems relating to the operation and 
maintenance of Bhakra-Nangal and Beas Projects. The said Committee issued some 
guidelines for filling of Bhakra and Pong Reservoirs. In accordance with these 
guidelines, the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) in the year 1990 decided 
that maximum level at Bhakra and Pong reservoirs should be kept 5 feet and  
10 feet below the designated FRL respectively, to provide cushion for possible floods. 
The operation of both the reservoirs is being done after discussing/ deliberating the 
same in the Technical Committee meeting(s) of BBMB which is represented by 
Chief Engineers of Irrigation Wing of partner States and the State Power utilities.
BBMB has developed Real Time Decision Support System (RTDSS) for efficient 
operation of reservoirs on river Satluj (Bhakra Dam) and river Beas (Pong Dam). 
BBMB has already installed Water Level Recording Stations in the catchment area 
of Satluj and Beas rivers. 
(c) to (e) Government of India has not given any directions to BBMB in this 
regard. However, the FRL of the Reservoirs had been fixed by taking informed 
decision in 138th and 139th Meeting of the BBMB by the Partner States keeping in 
view the reports of the Committee constituted for the said purpose after devastating 
floods of 1988.

Utilisation of water resources
2707. DR. VIKAS MAHATME:  Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION be pleased to state:
(a) the recommendations of the inter-Ministry Task Group on efficient utilisation 
of water resources and whether they have been accepted and implemented by 
Government; 
(b) whether the participatory irrigation management has achieved the objectives 
for which it was set up and whether the same has been reviewed in the recent past; 
(c) whether free power to agriculture is resulting in over exploitation of 
groundwater; and 
(d) if so, the details of the steps initiated to curb over exploitation of precious 
groundwater resources?

294 Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques...  [RAJYA SABHA] ...for the 19 March, 2018
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION (SHRI ARJUN RAM 
MEGHWAL): (a) The erstwhile Planning Commission in August 2004 constituted an 
Inter Ministry Task Group on Efficient Utilization of Water Resources to address the 
issues of over exploitation of ground water and non-utilization of created capacity 
and plan for efficient and optimal use of water resources. The recommendations of 
this Task Group are as below:–
A multipronged action plan encompassing both supply side augmentation and 
demand side management is called for, covering completion of ongoing storage 
projects taking up new storage works, inter-linking of rivers, modernization of existing 
irrigation systems, restoration of water bodies, bridging gap between potential created 
and potential utilized, participatory irrigation management, bench marking, ex-post 
facto evaluation of completed projects, development of groundwater in potential areas, 
artificial recharge of groundwater, prevention of overuse of groundwater, promotion 
of conjunctive use, tapping of the dynamic groundwater resources, micro irrigation 
especially for horticulture crops, strengthening of extension activities, S&T inputs, water 
audit in urban areas, institutional strengthening and setting up on an incentive fund.
Many of the recommendations of the Task Group were incorporated in the  
11th and Twelfth Five Year Plans.
(b) Participatory Irrigation Management (PIM) has been conceived as the thrust 
area in effective irrigation management by involving and associating farmers in 
planning, operation and maintenance of the irrigation systems. In April, 1987, the 
Ministry of Water Resources had issued guidelines for farmers participation under 
CADWM programme. Recognizing the need for sound legal framework for PIM in 
the country, during 1998, the Ministry brought out and circulated a model act to be 
adopted by the States legislatures for enacting new irrigation acts/amending existing 
irrigation acts. In accordance with the Model Act, 16 States have enacted legislation 
for involvement of farmers in irrigation management at different levels. Water Users’ 
Association have been formed by most of the States either through enactment of 
new irrigation acts or through various State Governments acts like Cooperative etc. 
prevailing in the States. The success of PIM intervention was reviewed in 2013 as 
a part of “Evaluation and Impact study of Command Area development and Water 
management Programme” carried out by Agricultural Finance Corporation Ltd.
(c) and (d) Ground water is being continuously extracted for various purposes 
including for irrigation in agriculture sector. Electricity subsidies are perceived to 
be one of the causes of groundwater overexploitation. Water being a State subject, 

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [20 March, 2018]   ...for the  19 March, 2018 295
respective State Governments are taking various measures to control over-exploitation 
of ground water resources. Several Steps also have been taken by Union Government 
to curb over-exploitation of ground water resources in the country. The Central 
Ground Water Authority (CGWA) constituted under Section 3(3) of ‘The Environment 
(Protection) Act, (1986)’ regulates extraction of ground water through guidelines which 
are updated regularly. Permission to extract ground water through any energized 
means is not accorded for any purpose other than drinking water in 162 notified 
areas. Government is also proposing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme named Atal 
Bhujal Yojana (ABHY) which aims to improve ground water management in select 
over-exploited and ground water stressed areas in identified priority States (Gujarat, 
Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh) 
through implementation of various interventions to ensure long-term sustainability of 
ground water resources with community participation.

Desiltation of rivers
2713. SHRI T. RATHINA VEL:  Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government is considering to enact a law on 
desiltation of rivers to prevent floods; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the proposed legislation would be drafted in 
consultation with the State Governments; 
(c) whether priority would be given for inter-linking of rivers; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES, 
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION (SHRI ARJUN RAM 
MEGHWAL): (a) and (b) No law on de-silting of rivers is under consideration/process 
in this Ministry. However, a draft Policy on Sediment Management has been prepared 
and circulated to all States/UTs and the concerned Central Ministries/Departments in 
August, 2017 seeking their views.
(c) and (d) Government of India has taken up the Interlinking of Rivers program 
on a high Priority and in a consultative mode. Under the National Perspective Plan 
for water resources development through inter basin transfer of water, for transferring 
water from water surplus basins to water-deficit basins, National Water Development 
Agency (NWDA) has identified 30 links (16 under Peninsular Component and 14 
under Himalayan Component) for preparation of Feasibility Reports. 
Four priority links for preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) under 
Peninsular Rivers Component have been identified viz. Ken-Betwa Link, Phase-I and 
II, Damanganga-Pinjal Link, Par-Tapi-Narmada link and Mahanadi-Godavari link. Based 
on the concurrence of the concerned States, Detailed Project Reports of Ken-Betwa 
link project Phase-I and Phase-II, Damanganga-Pinjal link and Par-Tapi-Narmada link 
have been completed.  

Written Ans. to Unstd. Ques... [20 March, 2018]   ...for the  19 March, 2018 307
The techno-economic clearance and various statutory clearances of the Ken-Betwa 
link project Phase-I have been accorded. Based on the request of State Government 
of Madhya Pradesh, the DPRs of projects included under Phase-II viz., Lower Orr 
dam, Bina Complex Projects and Kotha Barrage have been completed by NWDA/ 
Government of Madhya Pradesh and are under techno-economic appraisal in Central 
Water Commission. The draft MoU for implementation of Ken-Betwa Link Project has 
been sent to State Government of Uttar Pradesh and State Government of Madhya 
Pradesh for concurrence. 
The techno-economic clearance to the Damanganga-Pinjal link project has also 
been accorded subject to statutory clearances. The DPR of Par-Tapi-Narmada link 
is under technical appraisal in Central Water Commission. The draft MoU for 
implementation of Damanganga-Pinjal link and Par-Tapi-Narmada Link (including 
the four intra-state link projects of Maharashtra State) has been sent to Maharashtra 
and Gujarat for concurrence.
For taking up the Detailed Project Report of the links viz., Mahanadi-Godavari 
link and Godavari (Inchampalli)-Krishna links, the consensus building with concerned 
States is under process. Pending consensus on Mahanadi-Godavari and Godavari 
(Inchampalli)-Krishna link projects, alternative studies to divert surplus waters of 
Godavari river to Cauvery river through Godavari (Akinepalli)-Cauvery (Grand Anicut) 
link project are being carried out.

Bagh drain, Kalkaji drain and Tehkhand Nala has been undertaken at a total cost

discussions are held with the State agencies to ensure result oriented and expeditious
